messages:
alex: Heads-up — we pushed nvidia-container-toolkit 1.12.0 as a canary to a subset of us-west2 GPU nodes ~5m ago. Seeing containers fail at startup complaining about missing libcuda/libnvidia-ml on a few hosts.
maya: ugh. error logs?
alex: paste: ```/usr/local/bin/containerd-shim: error while loading shared libraries: libcuda.so.1: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory```
sam: are these nodes running the new kernel build from last week?
alex: most are on kernel 5.15.90, a handful on 5.19 in the same pool (mixed image rollout). failure concentrated on 5.19 hosts.
devon: infra-bot shows the canary set includes 4 hosts with 5.19. rolling back those hosts now?
infra-bot: :information_source: Deployment canary paused by infra-bot for artifacts: libcuda bind mount failed on 4/12 hosts.
maya: can we hotfix by adding explicit host bind-mounts for /usr/lib/nvidia* into the container runtime config?
sam: that masks the root cause. sounds like toolkit 1.12 changed mount propagation or relies on symlink layout that our image doesn't have.
devon: quick workaround: add an init script to symlink expected libs into /usr/local/nvidia and enable shared rbind on the shim. run command on affected hosts: ```for p in /usr/lib/nvidia*; do mount --bind $p /var/lib/containerd/nvidia$(basename $p); done``` but it's ugly.
alex: doing that on 4 hosts now to stabilize. we should pause the canary and mark the image as blocked.
maya: can we confirm NCCL tests still pass? these missing libs will break distributed jobs.
sam: ran a smoke NCCL allreduce on a recovered host — it fails with plugin init error, backtrace references libnvidia-ml.
devon: action items: 1) pause canary (done) 2) rollback toolkit to 1.11 on remaining hosts 3) run kernel+toolkit compatibility matrix across 5.15/5.19 4) audit container images for symlink expectations 5) notify ML teams.
alex: rolling back remaining canary hosts to 1.11, ETA ~18m.
infra-bot: :warning: Rollback started for toolkit 1.12 -> 1.11 on 8 hosts (triggered by alex).
maya: also add a preflight check in our upgrade job: verify libcuda resolves inside a scratch container before flipping the pool.
sam: +1. then we can detect these coupling issues before rollout. also think about pinning node base images per fleet to avoid mixed-kernel surprises.
devon: cost note — the failed containers triggered node restarts and a spike in transient autoscaler activity; expectation: ~0.3% extra infra cost this week. will add to incident.
alex: noted. I'll draft a short postmortem and include the workaround commands and tests. tagging @ml-platform for visibility.
maya: thanks — once rollback finishes, let's do canary again but with narrower kernel set and the preflight check enabled. :thumbsup:
